action.calculation: owner.currentMaxHp*ratio; current scoped source and target coincide

normalAttackElement.mechanism: native basic attack EP node, independent from ordinary HP damage node

evidence.claim: Revive declares MOVE_SPEED=6, MULTIPLIER=1, loadFromBlackboard=true with revive.move_speed5. The previously recovered common attribute formula uses 1+sum(multiplier), so this Buff contributes +500%, alone x6.

Both Scream selectors own an enabled CircleCollider2D with radius2.5 and offset0. All local scales along each original parent transform chain are1. Selector has no target count limit and honors range.

Self-damage is periodic1s with waitFirstInterval=true; named ScreamAttack trigger periodic1s with waitFirstInterval=false, castDirectly=true, checkCanUseAblityFlag=false. Both providers are mode1 owned and source templates are complete.

DamageViaMaxHpRatio.Execute gets current maxHP, reads ratio, multiplies them, and with an existing source and noSourceDamage=false invokes CalculateDamageByAtkWithSourceNoOnCalDmg. It propagates ignoreForSp and skipModifierEvent and allows lethal damage because isUndeadable=false. Here source, target and maxHP owner coincide.

AbstractBasicAttack.DoSetData loads EP ratio and independently creates its EP action branch when positive. ApplyElementDamage invokes a separate CalculateElementDamage formula and creates an elemental modifier; its source path reads attack rather than reusing the final ordinary HP damage packet.

Scream sourceAttackType2 is SPLASH and elementType1 is SANITY. Ordinary combat sourceAttackType1 is NORMAL, with SANITY EP loaded via EpDamage talent attack@ep_damage_ratio. There is no ON_OUTPUT_DAMAGE listener in either complete dslntc template.

Use the existing elemental packet rule attack*epRatio independent of ordinary DEF/RES mitigation; this is consistent with the separate native EP node path but the three native CalculateElementDamage bodies are unreadable. Exact original elemental resistance/EP modifier formula is not reconstructed by this contract.

The immediate ScreamAttack callback executes a zero-duration non-animated action once at each periodic trigger, independently from the normal attack lane. TriggerAbility.Execute is unreadable; exact internal castDirectly scheduling/interrupt behavior is not claimed reconstructed.

Mode1 providers attach once on mode entry, timers and modifiers are removed on mode exit, and each fresh entry starts its own configured periodic clocks. Native base detach remains the previous known boundary.

corrections: The old frozen awake contract mentioned x5 in its mode1 remaining-work summary. This new contract corrects it to MULTIPLIER +5 -> base*(1+5), without changing the old contract hash.
Do not infer attribute enum values from field declaration order. All included small integral enums were decoded from actual compressed metadata field defaults.
Do not convert zero HP atkScale into zero EP or apply a minimum ordinary damage floor to the zero-damage Scream action.
Do not add an ON_OUTPUT_DAMAGE listener: normal EP is native basic-attack configuration.
remainingBoundaries: Original BattleFormula.CalculateElementDamage three overloads unreadable after one targeted attempt; no retries.
Original TriggerAbility.Execute and MeleeAttack.DoSetData unreadable after one targeted attempt; parent AbstractBasicAttack source path retained.
Source CircleCollider2D radius2.5 is verified; a runtime center-distance test is a simulation mapping, not proof of exact original collision overlap at the edge.
Mode provider timer reset/removal and mid-battle save representation are shared runtime conventions, not original client field layouts.
validationRecommendations: At mode1 entry apply moveSpeed multiplier once: base.3 becomes1.8; exit returns original, no repeated x6 compounding.
Self-damage does not occur before1s, uses changed maxHP on later events and can kill; kill cancels further group emissions.
Scream first trigger follows waitFirstInterval=false, each tick hits every eligible target in2.5 range once, emits SANITY only, no HP damage floor.
Increasing target DEF/RES changes ordinary physical HP damage but not shared-runtime raw EP packet; report this as engine contract validation, not original formula proof.
Save/restore preserves timer elapsed state without replaying initial emission or double-applying stats.
Normal EP uses attack@ep_damage_ratio.1, not Scream.2, and there is no additional output-damage listener.
